claim: Practice hours explain a minority of skill variance in the 2014 meta-analysis: 12% overall as first published, 14% after the 2018 corrigendum (games 26 to 24, music 21 to 23, sports 18 to 20, education 4 to 5, professions under 1 to 1). The ordering games/music/sports well above education/professions is stable.
schema_part: G (calibration: more rehearsal does not fix everything)
agent_test: Quote both published and corrigendum values; use corrigendum values in schema notes.

claim: Domain regularity moderates the link: 24% for high-predictability activities, 12% moderate, 4% low (coder-rated, confounded with domain). LLM analogue (not the same thing): Snell 2024 finds the best test-time strategy depends on estimated question difficulty.
agent_test: Tag items by predictability; compare the gain of practice-style loops (retry with feedback) on regular vs open tasks at equal tokens.

claim: At the elite level hours barely separate performers: the sports meta-analysis gives 1% for national level and above (r=.11, 6 effects, N=228, not significant); all sports 18% as published (20% after corrigendum).
schema_part: G (diminishing returns of repetition at the top)
agent_test: On a hard-tail item set, check whether extra same-type sampling (best-of-N) adds nothing beyond the strongest tier.

claim: The measurement method changes the number: interview 20%, questionnaire 12%, log 5%; group-membership outcomes 26% vs standardized objective score 8%. Part of the headline link may come from recall bias and extreme-group designs.
schema_part: none (methods warning for our own evals)
agent_test: Avoid extreme-group contrasts in agent evals; use continuous scores and logged effort.

claim: The Ericsson 1993 violin result replicated only partly: the best-vs-good difference vanished (8,224 vs 9,844 h to age 18, d=-0.38, p=.364) while good-vs-less-accomplished held (d=1.33). Group effect eta2=.26 vs the original 48% of variance. Confirmed in full text this session.
agent_test: Pattern is a threshold effect: practice separates tiers but not the top two. Use as a prior when designing plateau checks.

claim: In the replication, weekly practice was higher for good than best violinists (30.65 vs 22.69 h, p=.024), and weekly estimates exceeded diary logs. Retrospective hour estimates are noisy.
agent_test: Prefer logged token and call counts over self-reported effort in agent studies.

claim: The size of the DP effect depends on definition. Ericsson and Harwell (2019) kept 14 of 88 studies and found r=.54 (29%), 61% after attenuation correction (r=.78). Critics show the corrected share swings 49% to 87% with assumed reliability .80 to .60, and that 7 of 8 DP effects came from studies Ericsson had rejected.
agent_test: Open definitional dispute. Our test must define practice operationally (targeted, with feedback) and measure it.

claim: In music, Platz et al. (2014) find a corrected r=.61 (37%, 13 studies, N=788) against Hambrick's 29.9% average; the gap comes from corrections and study selection. Both agree practice is the largest single measured predictor.
agent_test: None. Record the disagreement over r vs r-squared and over corrections.

claim: In chess hours explain about a third of variance (34%, 6 studies, N=533), and individual spread is huge: masters needed 832 to 24,284 h; 31% of masters had less than the expert-group mean.
schema_part: G (a fixed budget does not guarantee a level)
agent_test: Plot the spread of tokens-to-solve across items; plan adaptive stopping, not a fixed dose.

claim: Other factors add beyond practice: working memory capacity adds 7.4% to sight-reading beyond practice (r=.003 with practice, no interaction); chess intelligence r=.24 (youth .32, adult .11).
agent_test: Test whether a larger working scratchpad helps independent of loop count.

claim: Twin evidence: practice does not remove genetic influence on musical ability (about 50% genetic; relative heritability rose with practice in 2024; MZ twins with different practice did not differ in ability in 2014).
agent_test: No agent analogue (no heredity). Caution against reading practice effects as causal.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Far transfer of trained skill is near zero against active controls (music 0.03 SD, working-memory training 0.05 SD, chess 0.10 SD in one study) but 0.25 SD against passive controls.
schema_part: G (no promise of transfer from practice on one domain)
agent_test: Practise on task family A; test on family B at equal tokens against an active control.

claim: Early skill predicts senior elite performance only weakly in sports: world-class adults had more multi-sport coach-led practice, later main-sport start and less main-sport practice than national-class (|d| 0.23 to 0.50); juniors show the opposite. Abstract-level read.
schema_part: G (junior gains do not predict final level)
agent_test: Do not choose a strategy on early-iteration gains alone; recheck at full budget.

claim: Targeted, teacher-designed practice beats unguided repetition, and LLM analogues agree: targeted training on weak skills (STAT, gains up to 7.5% on MATH) and stronger-model or human feedback beat self-feedback. Abstract-level reads.
schema_part: O (targeted retry with an external signal)
agent_test: Compare self-critique retry vs retry with an external check at equal tokens.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an outside signal does not reliably help LLMs; gains appear when an oracle, tests or a reward exist, or when weights are trained for it. Abstract-level reads. Full texts now read: Huang 2023 intrinsic GSM8K 75.9 -> 74.7 over 5 calls; SCoRe table shows base model second attempt 41.4% vs first 52.6%.
schema_part: G (no unverified self-edit loops); O (verify with an external check)
agent_test: Run retry loops with and without an executable check; count net right-to-wrong flips.

claim: Self-improvement loops have ceilings: self-training is bounded by the data distribution (SPIN), RLVR improves pass@1 but may narrow pass@k, recursive synthetic data collapses. Support is mixed and abstract-level.
agent_test: Measure pass@k vs pass@1 for the scaffold against the base at equal tokens.

claim: In games, data volume (10M chess games, up to 270M parameters, Elo 2895) lifts models far, consistent with practice explaining most in rule-bound domains; but adversarial policies beat superhuman Go AIs (over 97% win), so volume leaves brittle holes.
agent_test: Treat as framing. Probe with adversarial items to find holes.

claim: No study found tests Ericsson-style deliberate-practice limits directly on an LLM; all LLM lines are analogies and mostly abstract-level reads. Closest indirect tests (full text): resampling coverage 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples (d07); self-repair no better than resampling at equal budget (d02).
agent_test: Design a direct test: dose-response of practice-style iterations on a fixed task family at equal tokens.

claim: AI-assisted practice among conservatory students (512 of 600 completed three waves) is observational and self-report, with no objective usage logs.
agent_test: None; weak evidence only.

claim: For LLMs, sequential self-repair iterations show strongly diminishing returns, while parallel resampling with a verifier keeps rising. Self-Refine per-iteration gains shrink (Constrained Generation 29.0 to 49.7 in 3 iterations, Code Optimization 22.0 to 28.8); s1 'Wait' scaling flattens near six times; repeated sampling gives 15.9% to 56% from 1 to 250 samples (SWE-bench Lite).
agent_test: At equal tokens, plot accuracy vs number of retries (1,2,3,5,8) for repair vs fresh sampling on one task family; find the knee.

claim: At equal sample budget, self-repair is often no better than fresh sampling, especially at small budgets; added repair attempts give marginal and sometimes negative gains, while more initial samples help consistently.
schema_part: G (budget-matched comparisons); O (verify with outside check)
agent_test: Report every retry result against a best-of-N control that uses the same number of calls.

claim: Routing by estimated difficulty beats a fixed strategy: compute-optimal allocation matched best-of-N with about 4x less test-time compute on MATH (PaLM 2-S*), and on the hardest bin no method made meaningful progress. The difficulty is model-estimated, not the human-rated predictability of K02.
schema_part: S0 (triage by difficulty); G (know when to stop)
agent_test: Estimate difficulty from a few cheap samples; light loops on easy items, resample on medium, stop or escalate on hardest. Compare to a fixed loop at equal tokens.

claim: Training on one task family transfers unevenly. In 20+ reasoning-tuned models most math gains did not carry to other domains; in a controlled Qwen3-14B math-only study RL generalised and SFT did not. Analogue of near-zero far transfer against active controls in humans (K12).
schema_part: G (no promise of transfer); memory-lesson reuse
agent_test: Store lessons from family A, run family B with and without them at equal tokens.

claim: An outside group (Debatin et al. 2023, N=178 chess players) finds the payoff of structured practice depends on individualization and teaching quality: interaction lifted R2 to .43 and the effect was over three times higher at +1 SD. This supports the definitional reading of K07 but is one correlational sample.
agent_test: Compare targeted vs generic feedback retries at equal tokens.

claim: Ability remains a predictor when exposure is controlled: in a trained-novice Rubik's cube study (N=79) fluid intelligence, not working memory or personality, predicted skill.
agent_test: Run the same scaffold on a weaker and a stronger base model; check whether the gain grows with base ability.
